title: Reefer Cargo Services: Terminal Plug-In Charges
content:
A laden Reefer Cargo Services unit is kept on terminal power at the port of loading until the vessel sails and again at the port of discharge until the container leaves the terminal. This page defines how those terminal days are counted and priced, when a service contract reduces the price, and when the charge may be booked.

## Clause

Plug-in is charged for every calendar day on which the laden reefer is plugged in, a started day counting as a full one. At the load terminal the stay runs from the plug-in date through the departure date; at the discharge terminal it runs from the discharge date through the delivery date; in both cases the first and the last day are each counted. From the days of each stay, the tier's free days for that terminal are deducted, and the days that remain are priced at the tier's daily rate for that terminal. The resulting charge for a stay is the number of remaining days multiplied by that daily rate, and it is nil when the free days equal or exceed the days of the stay. Each terminal stay gives rise to one charge of its own.

When the customer holds a service contract that is active and whose tier rank is at or above the qualifying rank set by the reefer tier, the plug-in charge is reduced by the tier's contract reduction percentage and the reduced amount is rounded to the cent; a qualifying rank of 0 means that no reduction is granted. Plug-in kept up at a transshipment port is part of the service and is not charged separately. A plug-in charge may be booked only once the service is in transit or delivered.

## Calculation guide for one terminal stay

1. Count the calendar dates of the stay, both ends included.
2. Deduct the tier's free days for that terminal, stopping at zero.
3. Multiply the remaining days by the tier's daily rate for that terminal.
4. Where the contract reduction applies, take the reduction percentage off that amount and round the result to the cent.

## Worked examples (hypothetical rates and dates)

- Imagine a daily load-terminal rate of 40.00 with one free day. A reefer plugged in on 3 May whose vessel sails on 7 May has five plug-in days (3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 May); one is free, four are charged, and the stay costs 160.00. Were the customer entitled to an imagined 5 percent reduction, the charge would become 152.00.
- Imagine a daily rate of 33.33 with no free day and a two-day stay: 66.66 before reduction. A 5 percent reduction leaves 63.327, which rounds to 63.33.
- Imagine two free days at discharge. A container discharged on 10 June and delivered on 12 June has three days at that terminal, of which one is charged.

## Points of judgement

- The load stay and the discharge stay are priced separately, each with its own rate and free days, and each is booked as its own charge.
- A service still plugged in at the load terminal, not yet sailed, cannot yet take a plug-in charge.
- The reduction turns on the customer's service contract standing together with the reefer tier's own qualifying rank and percentage, and it is a reduction of plug-in charges.
